construct: KRT6A encodes keratin 6a, which heteropolymerizes with keratin 16 to form epithelial intermediate filaments; pathogenic variants disrupt filament assembly and mechanical resilience, producing nail dystrophy, painful plantar keratoderma, friction blisters, and oral leukokeratosis.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Childhood hypertrophic nail dystrophy, painful plantar keratoderma, friction-induced blisters, oral leukokeratosis, autosomal-dominant family history, and a KRT6A variant identify pachyonychia congenita; keratin 6a is an intermediate-filament protein.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Actin filaments and microtubules are intracellular cytoskeletal systems but are not built from keratin 6a. Type I collagen fibrils and fibrillin microfibrils are extracellular matrix structures, whereas KRT6A encodes an epithelial keratin that assembles into intracellular intermediate filaments.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The supplied gene makes the structural mapping exact: KRT6A is a keratin gene, and keratins constitute epithelial intermediate filaments; none of the alternative structural networks is encoded by KRT6A.
